name: American BBQ: Smoked Shredded Chicken Thighs
description: Skinless chicken thighs rubbed and rested in the fridge, smoked at 110°C, sprayed with apple cider vinegar, wrapped after an hour and finished hotter at 150°C until 90°C inside, then shredded in their juices.
recipeIngredient: 1-1.5 kg chicken thighs, skin off (bone-in or boneless)
## Rub (half batch of the Memphis pulled pork rub)
apple cider vinegar, in a spray bottle
mild fruit wood chunks (apple or cherry)
splash of apple juice or cider, for wrapping
BBQ sauce or Memphis mop sauce

itemListElement.text: Mix the rub ingredients. Pat the thighs dry, apply the rub evenly all over, and leave them in the fridge for 2 hours.
Prepare the BBQ for indirect heat at about 110°C. Wait until the charcoal ashes over, stir, then pile for indirect cooking.
Put the chicken in. Add just enough wood to smoke for the first 30 minutes only; chicken takes smoke quickly and fruit wood is milder.
Spray lightly with apple cider vinegar while smoking to keep the surface moist.
After 1 hour, wrap the thighs tightly in a foil pan or double foil with a knob of butter and a splash of apple juice or cider (Texas crutch).
Turn the heat up to about 150°C after wrapping to speed up the cook, and return the wrapped chicken to the BBQ.
Cook until the thighs reach 90°C inside and the probe slides in with almost no resistance. Remove at 90°C.
Rest in the wrap for 15-20 minutes.
Remove any bones, tip the meat and juices into a bowl and pull apart with two forks. Toss in the juices, season with salt, and add BBQ sauce or mop sauce if you like.
Serve on bread rolls with cabbage and apple slaw.
